{"id": "c59c236d-6856-4682-ada8-b7a467ad8669", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"type": "chat_title", "title": "Resizing EBS gp3 volume IOPS with CLI"}]}

{"id": "2896d699-af15-444e-9fde-1adc2c81927a", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "To change IOPS on a gp3 volume, use `modify_volume` in the EC2 API. Here's the general form:

```bash
aws ec2 modify-volume \
    --volume-id vol-xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx \
    --iops 6000
```

A few notes:
- gp3 volumes support provisioned IOPS from 3,000 (baseline, included free) up to 16,000.
- You can also adjust `--size` (GiB) or `--volume-type` in the same call if needed.
- Check progress with `aws ec2 describe-volumes-modifications --volume-ids vol-xxxxxxxxxxxxxxxxx` — modifications are gradual and the volume stays in-use/available during the process.
- There's a cooldown: after modifying a volume, you generally need to wait at least 6 hours before the next modification (unless the previous one didn't change size, IOPS, or throughput).

Want me to check the current IOPS/throughput configuration on one of your actual volumes, or run the modification for you?", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
